And we'll go over this next class. Okay, so Solomon is the son of David who becomes king. They know what happened with Bathsheba and Abner. Gossiping causes problems for the king. You need to spin this or tell the story in a different way that makes the gossiping less bad. The gossiping right now is that David killed Uriah because Uriah was a threat. If people believe this, it's possible that Uriah's friends will want revenge and a soldier might try to kill David because he's ambitious. So you change the gossip to say David was not ambitious; he was just a poet who fell in love with Bathsheba. This makes people think David is irresponsible but infallible, which is better than thinking he's a ruthless killer.

In the Bible, this spin changes the narrative from David being a ruthless killer to him making mistakes and needing forgiveness. People should forgive David because Yahweh also makes mistakes and needs forgiveness. Now you switch the story to say it was really about Bathsheba and that people make mistakes; we should forgive them. This is why the Bible was created to change gossip so it would be less harmful.

You don't want people thinking David killed Uriah because he saw Uriah as a threat, which might lead people to think David also had to kill Saul. So you switch the story to say no, it was just about Bathsheba. Writing does three things: legitimacy, unity, and differentiation. Legitimacy means this guy should be the king because that's the will of God. Unity means we are one family with the same values. Differentiation means our god is different from other gods; Yahweh is a god of forgiveness, fallibility, reflection, and debate.

Our god is good, we're just one family with one history, and David is a poet king which is why Yahweh favors him. The Bible was constructed as propaganda to use opportunity to create beautiful stories that become living entities and ignite the imagination of the Jewish people. This creativity is why the Jewish people are so creative.

Next class, we'll do the Persians. The Jews, the Greeks, and the Persians are the three most creative peoples of this period and pillars of Western civilization.
